title: Interaction Transfer to Unseen Scientific Entities
description:
Research code and committed evidence for studying when pair-specific interaction effects transfer from observed combinations to unseen scientific entities.

The outcome of combining two entities is decomposed as y(i,j) = f(i) + f(j) + I(i,j), and the project asks when the pair term I generalises across three regimes of increasing difficulty: an unseen combination of seen entities, a combination involving one entity never observed, and a combination in which neither entity was observed.

Evaluated on two external systems: the Koplev sequential anticancer drug screen, where the directional effect splits exactly into a generic ordering potential and a pair-specific cyclic component that is predictable for unseen pairs above a coverage threshold; and the ChemLex acid-amine coupling high-throughput screen, where the interaction is bipartite and the first detectable both-reactants-unseen result was obtained on a single-condition screen.

Includes a falsification study that runs the published estimator which produced the drug-screen target on simulated screens containing no pair-specific interaction, four pre-registered decision rules published verbatim, and an explicit record of the claims that were withdrawn. Two of the four registered rules returned INCONCLUSIVE; both the frozen verdicts and the corrected post-hoc readings are reported. This is a research artifact and has not been peer reviewed.
